title: Daan Tat: Hong Kong Egg Tarts with Flaky Pastry
summary: Flaky laminated pastry cases filled with a silky sugar-water and evaporated milk custard, baked until just set.
equipment: 16 egg tart moulds (7 cm) or a 12-hole plus 4-hole muffin tin

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Make the butter layer
steps.text: Pulse the 170 g flour with the cold butter in the food processor to a smooth paste. Scrape it onto cling film, pat into a 12 cm square, wrap and chill for 30 min.

steps.title: Make the water dough
steps.text: Pulse the 180 g flour with the sugar and salt, add the yolk and cold water and pulse until it clumps. Knead briefly into a ball, flatten into a rectangle, wrap and chill for 30 min.

steps.title: Enclose the butter
steps.text: Roll the water dough to a 25 cm square. Place the butter square on it at an angle, like a diamond, fold the four corners over to meet in the middle and pinch the seams to seal.

steps.title: Fold for layers
steps.text: Roll into a 40 x 15 cm strip, fold both short ends in to meet in the centre, then close it like a book. Turn 90° and repeat. Chill for 30 min, give it one more roll and book fold, then chill for at least 1 h. These folds build the flaky layers.

steps.title: Mix the custard
steps.text: Stir the sugar into the hot water until dissolved and let it cool a little. Whisk in the evaporated milk, eggs, yolks, vanilla and salt, then strain into the jug and chill while you shape the cases. Straining gives the smooth, glassy top.

steps.title: Shape the cases
steps.text: Halve the pastry and roll each piece to about 3 mm thick. Cut 8 circles from each half and press them into the greased moulds so the pastry rises a few millimetres above the rim. Prick the bases and freeze for 20-30 min.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan). Put the cold cases on the tray, fill them almost to the top with custard and bake for 16-20 min, turning the tray halfway, until the pastry is golden and the custard is set with just a faint wobble.

steps.title: Cool and unmould
steps.text: Leave the tarts in their moulds for 5 min, then ease them out and serve warm.

tips: A common mistake is overbaking: the custard puffs, then sinks and cracks. Take them out while there is still a slight wobble.
Keep the pastry cold throughout; if the butter softens, chill it for 15 min before carrying on.
Fill the cases straight from the freezer so the pastry holds its shape.
Skim any bubbles off the custard before baking for a mirror-smooth top.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best eaten warm on the day. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge for up to 2 days and warm at 180 °C (160 °C fan) for 5 min.
